---
title: "Exercise 1a: Variables & variable types"
---

::: {.milestone}
**Block 1** · Learning goals: Make a new Python program, nnderstand what a variable is in Python & different types of variables.  
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Make a new Python program & save the file"}

Create a new Python code file in the Coder on UCloud.

Save the file in /work/cogsci_methods01_e26 (or whatever you have named your methods cosgci folder).

:::

Now complete the following coding exercises in this file. 

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Make a variable and inspect its value in the console"}

Make any variable of any type.

Print the value of the variable to the console.

Add a comment above the variable to describe it.

Print the variable type to the console. 

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Data Type 1: Regular string variables"}

Print the character string "Null hypothesis: Eating ice cream does not improve mood"

Store this expression in a variable called `null_hypothesis`

Print the first four characters of this string variable. 

Print the last four characters of this string variable. 

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="String methods"}

Split the variable `null_hypothesis` by spaces and store the output in a new variable called `split_var`. 

Print split_var[1]`  to the console. What is the output? 
Can you explain what function of the square brackets is? 
And the index inside of them? 

Can you index the second character in split_var[1]?

Split the string variable by the colon (:) character and store the output in a new variable.

Replace the lower case h in the `null_hypothesis` character string with an upper case H. 

Index the word 'hypothesis' in the `split_var` variable and store the output in a new variable called `hypothesis_word`

Convert `hypothesis_word` to all upper case characters and store in a new variabled called `hypothesis_word_upper`

Replace the word 'hypothesis' in the variable `null_hypothesis` with `hypothesis_word_upper`

Test whether `hypothesis_word_upper` starts with `H`

Get the length of `null_hypothesis`

There's lots more that you can do with strings, but these are the basics!

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Data Type 2: Regular numeric variables"}

Make a variable containing an integer. 

Make a floating point variable. 

Print the types of these two variables. 

Add the two variables. What happens?

Subtract the two variables. What happens?

Divide the two variables.

Multiply the two variables and store the output in a new variable. 

::: 

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Printing variables"}

Imagine that you want to print reaction times for a given subject on an experiment screen.

The subject is different in each experiment, and so is their reaction time. 

Print an expression to the screen that says "The current subject is " and insert the current subject's ID.

Print an expression to the screen that says "The current subject is [insert their ID] and their reaction time is [insert their reaction time]"

:::
